newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 30.

text.p: Following are the highlights of
the Irish press on Wednesday:
IRISH TIMES
- Aid agency Goal to co-operate in a department of foreign
affairs audit
- Finance minister Charlie McCreevy to limit tax cuts because of
inflation fears
- Ireland's Supreme Court to hear U2 concerts appeal today
- Belfast man beaten for 'joyriding' was driven to suicide, says
father
- Irish pound back over 90 pence as selling weakens sterling
- EU to re-allocate 120 million punts of the Republic's
structural funding
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- Race to save 150 million punts as EU warns on spending
- Aid agency Goal backs down on funding row
- Dublin stands to lose an estimated 10 million and see its
reputation as a major internatinal music centre badly dented if
the U2 concerts do not go ahead
- Bord Failte not consulted on decision to scrap new logo
- Golden Vale bounces back with 6.5 million punts half-year
profits
- Auditors of financier Dermot Desmond's personal office block
at the IFSC have warned him that losses of over 6.0 million
punts mean that it may not be appropriate to treat IFSC South
Block Ltd accounts on a going concern basis
- Intel cuts prices by 57 percent
- Warning by Statoil on Connemara oil hopes
THE EXAMINER
- Workers demand extra 2.0 percent in pay packets as the economy
continues to surge
- Triple killer O'Donnell is cremated in quiet service
- Health minister will meet McCole family to discuss Hepetitis C
report
